title: PLA vs PETG
caption: PLA vs PETG: which filament wins? #3dprinting #pla #petg #filament

beats.line: Which filament should you pick for your next print?

beats.label: ROUND 1
beats.line: Round one, strength. PETG flexes and takes a beating while PLA stays stiff.

beats.label: ROUND 2
beats.line: Round two, ease. PLA prints cleanly with less fuss and almost no stringing.
Round three, heat. PETG handles a warm car far better than PLA.
For tough everyday parts that live outside, choose PETG.

title: Fix stringing
caption: Stop stringing in three quick fixes. #3dprinting #stringing #troubleshooting

beats.line: Is your print covered in spiderweb strings? Here is the quick fix.
First, wet filament is the usual culprit, so dry your spool.
Second, too much heat makes the nozzle ooze, so lower the temperature.
Third, turn on retraction so the filament pulls back before every travel move.
Fix those three and your surface comes out clean and smooth.

title: Three first layer tips
caption: Three tips for a perfect first layer. #3dprinting #firstlayer #tips

beats.line: Want a perfect first layer every single time? Try these three tips.

beats.label: TIP 1
beats.line: Tip one, level your bed so the nozzle height is even.

beats.label: TIP 2
beats.line: Tip two, clean the plate with soap so the plastic sticks properly.

beats.label: TIP 3
beats.line: Tip three, slow down the first layer so every line lays down smoothly.
Do all three and your prints will stick for the whole job.

Corners lifting off the bed? That is warping, and it is fixable.
Cold drafts shrink the plastic unevenly, so shield your printer from air.
A warm bed keeps the bottom layers gripping, so heat it properly.
A brim adds extra grip around the edges where the lifting starts.
Combine all of these and those corners stay flat and tight.

Meet flexible filament, the rubbery material that bends without breaking.
Its biggest strength is toughness, perfect for phone cases and soft grips.
The weakness is speed, because it must print slow and gentle.
Best uses are bumpers, gaskets and anything that needs to bounce back.
Keep the spool dry and use a direct drive extruder for the best results.

Rough print to showroom finish in three simple steps.
Step one, sand the layer lines with coarse paper, then move to fine.
Step two, spray a thin coat of primer to fill the tiny gaps.
Step three, paint in light coats and let each one dry fully.

beats.label: PATIENCE
beats.line: Be patient, because rushing the drying is how mistakes happen.

title: Matte vs silk
caption: Matte vs silk filament, who wins? #3dprinting #silk #matte

beats.line: Matte or silk, which finish will win on your shelf today?

beats.label: ROUND 1
beats.line: Round one, looks. Silk shines and sparkles under every light.

beats.label: ROUND 2
beats.line: Round two, hiding flaws. Matte hides layer lines far better.

beats.label: ROUND 3
beats.line: Round three, printing ease. Matte is forgiving, silk likes slow speeds.
For display models and gifts, silk steals the show.
For everyday parts, matte wins. Follow for more finish battles!
